title: Breadth-First Search Step-by-Step
description: Advance breadth-first search one ring at a time and predict which vertices it must visit next.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Graph Theory Fundamentals

educational.learningObjective: Given a starting vertex, the learner will predict which vertex breadth-first search visits next at each step, based on hop distance from the start.
prerequisites: Knows what a vertex and an edge are
Can follow a path through a graph
learningOutcomes: Predict the next vertices BFS will visit
Recognize that BFS computes shortest hop distances as a side effect
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Point at a vertex mid-traversal and ask the learner whether BFS visits it on the next step, with a justification in terms of hop distance.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Stepwise algorithm walkthrough with prediction prompts
pedagogical.feedbackType: Ring-by-ring coloring, distance labels, and a named prediction for the next step
misconceptionsAddressed: That BFS follows one path to its end before backtracking
That the drawn length of an edge affects traversal order
discussionQuestions: Why does BFS find shortest paths while depth-first search does not?
What does hop distance mean in a social network? In a supply chain?
Where have you seen 'degrees of separation' used as a real measure?
